solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wild call by card player after ace and king turned over

indicators.note: coming after means being placed later in the line, so one piece follows the other
something turned over ends up facing the other way, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace
R stands for Rex, Latin for king
at bridge a player makes a call by bidding

explanation.surface: A bridge player makes a reckless call after an ace and a king are revealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild call' reads as one phrase, but 'Wild' stands alone as the definition. R for king comes from the Latin Rex, as in the royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabid supporter is fanatical and frenzied, so the word works as a synonym for uncontrolled or crazed.

clue.text: Extremely angry, missing European racing event

indicators.note: whatever is missing has been left out, so a letter drops from the phrase

parts.note: an intensifier meaning very
cross means annoyed
E is the abbreviation for European; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: Someone is furious at being left out of a European motor race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely angry' reads as a phrase, and it is: REALLY CROSS, from which the E goes to leave RALLYCROSS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rallycross is a form of motor sport where cars race around a mixed tarmac and gravel circuit.

clue.text: Again relative turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning something up means reading it from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: sib is short for sibling

explanation.surface: A family member has shown up yet again.
explanation.walkthrough: BIS is a Latin word used in music and by audiences calling for a repeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Bis means twice or once more, used in scores to show a passage should be repeated.

clue.text: Face up to work and discussion at the White House

parts.note: a dial is the face of a clock or watch

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to go is to work or function, as a machine does

explanation.surface: Confronting some tough political talks in Washington.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face up to' looks like one idiom meaning confront, but 'Face' and 'up' work separately. 'At the White House' signals the American spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialog is the American spelling of dialogue, a conversation or exchange of views between parties.

clue.text: Brother wearing several reduced pink hats

indicators.note: to wear something is to be inside it, so one piece sits within another
reduced means cut down, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: some means a few, several
rose is a pink colour; the last letter goes
BR is the abbreviation for brother

explanation.surface: A monk has on a handful of faded pink hats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pink hats' looks like a description, but pink is a colour word that loses a letter, and the definition is 'hats' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A sombrero is a broad-brimmed Mexican hat, so the plural is simply a set of hats.

clue.text: In flames? I lit match

indicators.note: lit is slang for drunk, and a drunk staggers about out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something is on fire, and the speaker admits to striking the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lit' and 'match' both seem to be about fire, but 'lit' means drunk and 'match' is a sporting fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A semifinal is the round of a knockout competition whose winners go through to the final fixture.

clue.text: Pole briefly working for builder

indicators.note: said briefly, a word is cut short and loses its last letter

parts.note: a mast is a tall pole; the last letter goes
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A Polish man is briefly employed by a builder.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital P makes 'Pole' look like a Polish person; it is a post or mast.
explanation.definitionFit: A mason is a craftsman who builds with stone or brick, so he is a kind of builder.

clue.text: Rescuer splashing about round pool

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes around another
splashing throws things about in disorder, so these letters get mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A lifeguard splashes around a swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pool' seems to be where the rescuer is splashing; it is the definition, in its sense of a shared supply.
explanation.definitionFit: A pool of money or labour is a shared stock to draw on, which is what a resource is.

clue.text: Substitute given stick after failing to finish second match

indicators.note: something that fails to finish stops short, so the word loses its last letter
coming after means placed later in the line, so one piece follows the other

parts.note: a replay is a match played again; the last letter goes
to cement is to stick things together

explanation.surface: A substitute is shown the stick for not completing a replayed game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Substitute' and 'match' suggest football, and 'stick' suggests criticism, but stick here means glue.
explanation.definitionFit: A substitute is someone or something that takes another's place, exactly what a replacement is.

clue.text: Father is up and about

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written
re means concerning, about

explanation.surface: Dad is out of bed and moving around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up and about' is a stock phrase for being out of bed; it splits into a reversal signal, a link and RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To sire offspring is to father them, and a sire is a male parent, especially of an animal.

clue.text: Girl swallows a minute drink over in island resort

indicators.note: whatever swallows something takes it inside, so one piece holds another

parts.note: a lass is a girl
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for minute

indicators.note: something turned over faces the other way, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: to lap is to drink as a cat does

explanation.surface: A girl downs a tiny drink while holidaying on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like an adjective for a small drink, but it is the unit of time, M.
explanation.definitionFit: Las Palmas is the capital of Gran Canaria in the Canary Islands, a popular holiday destination.

clue.text: Taste no end of wine from South Africa

indicators.note: with no end, a word loses its final letter

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Africa
port is a fortified wine; the last letter goes

explanation.surface: Sampling endless South African wine.
explanation.walkthrough: SAPOR is a rare literary word from Latin; the wordplay spells it out even if it is unfamiliar.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapor is a formal word for flavour, the quality perceived by the tongue and palate.

clue.text: Fish an unfit cooked accompaniment for chicken

indicators.note: an accompaniment goes alongside something, so one piece sits next to the other

parts.note: chicken and yellow both mean cowardly

indicators.note: cooking transforms raw ingredients, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fish that is unfit to eat is cooked and served with chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken' and 'cooked' paint a kitchen, but chicken means cowardly here.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellowfin tuna is a large ocean species caught widely for food, so it is a kind of fish.

clue.text: Tenant thrown out in Leeds and Lahore

indicators.note: things thrown out land scattered, so these letters come out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tenants are being evicted in both a Yorkshire city and a Pakistani one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrown out' fits the eviction story perfectly, which hides its job as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaseholder occupies property under a lease from the owner, which is what a tenant does.

clue.text: Talks will enthral daughter beginning to study game of strategy

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: talks given to audiences are speeches
D is the abbreviation for daughter

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of study

explanation.surface: Lectures captivate a daughter as she starts studying a strategy game.
explanation.walkthrough: The daughter goes into the talks, and the first letter of study is tacked on at the very end.
explanation.definitionFit: Speed chess is chess played with very short time limits, still a board game of tactics and planning.

clue.text: Way American woman ignores British

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: broad is American slang for a woman
B is the abbreviation for British; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: The American way is for a woman to ignore the British.
explanation.walkthrough: BROAD is dated American slang for a woman; dropping B for British leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A way is a route or path to travel along, and a road is the commonest example.

clue.text: At little cost, fellow twice visits parts of Acton with a bit of cash

indicators.note: a visitor goes into a place, so one piece is put inside another
with means alongside, so one piece is added next to the rest
a word broken into parts can be put back together in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
he is a male fellow, taken twice
P is a penny, a small unit of British money

explanation.surface: A man makes two trips to parts of Acton carrying only a little money.
explanation.walkthrough: Acton is a district of west London. 'Parts of' breaks its letters up and rearranges them, with the two fellows slotted in among them.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means cheaply or spending as little as possible, the same as at low expense.

clue.text: Hard work removing railway covering an Asian region

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece covering another sits on top of it, so it comes first

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: removing something takes it away, so letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: industry is diligent work
RY is the abbreviation for railway; these letters are removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Heavy labour clearing a railway line in part of Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard work' reads as one phrase, but it splits into H and INDUSTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindustan is an old name for northern India, or the whole subcontinent, a large area of Asia.

clue.text: Deduction in pay for refusal to work

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an amount stopped from wages
second meaning: a strike or walkout

explanation.surface: Workers are docked wages for going on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings form a plausible cause and effect, which makes the clue look like one definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both money held back from wages and industrial action halting work.

clue.text: Cause of beastly smell, namely, that primarily is found in the country

parts.note: SC abbreviates scilicet, Latin for namely

indicators.note: something found in a place is inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: the country in a British newspaper

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of that

explanation.surface: The source of an animal odour turns out to be rural.
explanation.walkthrough: SC for namely is short for the Latin scilicet. In a British paper, 'the country' is usually England.
explanation.definitionFit: A scent gland is an organ in many mammals that secretes strong-smelling musk for marking territory.

clue.text: Fine weather intermittently for outdoor event

parts.note: F is the pencil abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: intermittently means on and off, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Hoping for occasional sunshine for a garden party.
explanation.walkthrough: A fete is a fair held outdoors to raise money, typical of an English village summer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is a public open-air festival with stalls and games, so it is a type of outdoor event.

clue.text: Award, one accepted by leader of rock group

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside another
the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of rock
I is the Roman numeral for one
a band is a musical group

explanation.surface: A rock band's frontman accepts an award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader of rock group' reads as a singer, but it splits into R and BAND, with I placed between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A riband is a ribbon, especially one given as a prize, as in the Blue Riband.

clue.text: Work left university staff mostly looking for a break

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
port is the left side of a ship
uni is short for university
a staff is a walking stick; the last letter goes

explanation.surface: Academics have walked out of work, hoping for a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work left' suggests people leaving jobs, and 'university staff' suggests lecturers, but each word is its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Being opportunistic means seizing chances as they arise, and a break is a lucky chance.

clue.text: I am outwardly ruddy frosty

indicators.note: outwardly means on the outside, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: ruddy means reddish in colour
I'm is the contraction of I am

explanation.surface: Someone looks red-faced but is cold at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruddy' can be a mild British swear word, so it looks like an intensifier for 'frosty'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rime is hoar frost, so something rimed is coated in ice crystals, that is, frosty.

clue.text: Exclamation of disgust, initially having drink upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, something upset is tipped over, so the letters run backwards
initially means at the start, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of having
to sip is to drink in small mouthfuls

explanation.surface: Someone snorts in disgust after spilling a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' fits the spilled drink and the disgust, but it signals reversal in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Pish is an old interjection voicing contempt or impatience, much like pshaw or bah.

clue.text: Deity behind rain, to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent means partly, so only part of the words is taken

parts.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Some god is partly responsible for the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes a neat joke: Indra really is the Hindu god of rain and thunder, so the clue is close to literally true.
explanation.definitionFit: Indra is the Vedic king of the gods in Hinduism, ruling sky, storms and rainfall.

clue.text: Got together and took single drug

parts.note: people who met got together
had can mean took, as in had a drink
one is a single unit

explanation.surface: People met up and each took one dose of a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took' seems to go with 'drug', but it is HAD, and the definition is the last word alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Methadone is a synthetic opioid medicine used for pain relief and in treating heroin addiction.

clue.text: Article encased in fine timber

indicators.note: something encased in a shell is surrounded by it, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: OK means fine, all right
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An object in a fine wooden case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine timber' reads as quality wood, but 'fine' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Oak is a hard, durable wood prized for furniture and building, a classic kind of timber.

clue.text: Herts town set welcoming writer

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one piece holds another

parts.note: to set is to harden, as concrete does
a pen is something that writes

explanation.surface: A town in Hertfordshire is ready to receive an author.
explanation.walkthrough: Herts is the standard abbreviation for Hertfordshire, a county just north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Harpenden is a commuter town in Hertfordshire, between St Albans and Luton.

clue.text: One who scored duck: caught out, say

indicators.note: when a player is out they leave, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught; this letter is removed
as means for example, like say

explanation.surface: A cricketer who made a duck, caught out for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero, so scoring a duck sounds like failing; 'scored' here means wrote music.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Dukas was a French composer, best known for The Sorcerer's Apprentice, so he scored music.
